_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and the input file x17-rc-input.json; no other repository file, search, web page or API was consulted.

hints.reason: ALIEN via the famous tagline 'In space no one can hear you scream'; VACUUM via the true reason, sound cannot travel through a vacuum, so the tagline itself ties both together.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent indirect aha; the tagline is widely quoted and the physics is true.

hints.reason: CATERPILLAR via The Very Hungry Caterpillar; APPLE via the book's first food (one apple on Monday), a detail most U.S. readers remember from the hole-punched page.

pairs.pair_note: Apple side leans on a book detail, but it is the iconic first page; facts are correct.

hints.reason: DWARF via Gimli, the Fellowship's dwarf; AXE via his signature weapon, both well known from the Lord of the Rings films.

pairs.pair_note: Solid character hint; requires knowing the films but they are mainstream.

hints.reason: BALCONY via the famous balcony scene; POISON via Romeo drinking poison at the tragic end.

pairs.pair_note: Classic, fair and satisfying.

hints.reason: BATH via Archimedes' bath-time 'Eureka!'; GOLD via both the gold crown in that legend and California's gold-rush motto 'Eureka'.
hints.fix: Archimedes is said to have shouted "Eureka!" in his bath when he realized how to test a gold crown, and "Eureka" is California's motto from its gold rush.

pairs.pair_note: Double route to GOLD makes this strong; the legend has him realizing the method in the bath, not testing the crown there.

hints.reason: JELLY via 'royal jelly'; BEE because royal jelly is the bee food that makes a queen, so ROYAL also echoes the queen bee.

pairs.pair_note: Royal jelly is familiar enough as a health-store product; text is accurate.

hints.reason: BIRD and WATCH together via birdwatching, the classic binoculars activity; WATCH alone is only the generic act of looking through them.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clear scene clue; WATCH is carried by the compound 'bird watching' rather than a standalone link.

hints.reason: BOARD via plank as a long board; PIRATE via walking the plank, with the explanation rightly framing it as 'in stories'.

pairs.pair_note: Synonym on one side, iconic pirate image on the other; satisfying.

hints.reason: BONE via breaking a bone; RECORD via breaking a record; clean double use of the verb.

pairs.pair_note: Simple and fair.

hints.reason: BRAIN via the cartoon Pinky and the Brain; FINGER via the pinky as the little finger.

pairs.pair_note: Fun pop-culture double meaning.

hints.reason: LOVE and BUG via Herbie's film The Love Bug; BUG also via Herbie being a VW Beetle, nicknamed a Bug.

pairs.pair_note: Older Disney reference but still widely known (and revived in 2005).

hints.reason: CAKE via icing on a cake; FROST via icing as frosting (to frost a cake), with icing/frost also sharing the ice sense.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, honest link; low delight but clear.

hints.reason: CAP via graduation 'cap and gown'; DRESS via a gown being a formal dress.

pairs.pair_note: Clean and fair.

hints.reason: CARPET via Princess Jasmine's magic-carpet ride in Aladdin; RICE via jasmine rice.

pairs.pair_note: Strong double meaning with a nice aha.

hints.reason: GOAT via the acronym Greatest Of All Time; CHAMPION via 'the greatest' as the label for top champions (Ali's 'I am the greatest').

pairs.pair_note: GOAT side is a real aha; champion side is a looser near-synonym but honest.

hints.reason: CHOCOLATE via Dove chocolate (Mars); SOAP via the Dove beauty bar; one brand name, two unrelated products.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent brand double; facts are correct.

hints.reason: CLOSET and MONSTER via Monsters, Inc., where Boo meets the monsters through her closet door; MONSTER also via 'boo' as the classic scare.

pairs.pair_note: Layered and satisfying; the monster-in-the-closet trope supports it even without the film.

hints.reason: COFFEE via Starbucks, named after Starbuck; WHALE via Starbuck as first mate of the Pequod hunting Moby Dick, a well-circulated naming fact.

pairs.pair_note: The whale side needs the Moby-Dick naming trivia, but it is widely repeated and the click is strong once seen.

hints.reason: COUNTRY and ROAD via John Denver's 'Take Me Home, Country Roads'; the hint first reads as the city, so the aha comes from switching to the singer.
hints.fix: "Take Me Home, Country Roads" is one of John Denver's best-known songs.

pairs.pair_note: Song is hugely familiar; the COUNTRY line's 'best-known' superlative is softened in the fix.

hints.reason: CROWN via corona as Latin for crown; VIRUS via coronavirus, named for its crown-like fringe of spikes.

pairs.pair_note: True and satisfying; pandemic context is widely known and PG.

hints.reason: PLAY via the idiom 'playing possum'; DEAD via opossums appearing dead when threatened, so the hint lands on 'play dead'.

pairs.pair_note: Neat: the hint reconstructs the targets' own phrase 'play dead'.

hints.reason: INTERNET via offline meaning no connection; DINOSAUR via Chrome's offline T. rex jumping game.

pairs.pair_note: Great modern aha that most players have seen.

hints.reason: TARGET via the bullseye at a target's center (and Target's logo); DOG via Bullseye, Target's dog mascot.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; uses both the object and the store sense of TARGET.

hints.reason: KING via Martin Luther King Jr.'s name; DREAM via his 1963 'I Have a Dream' speech.

pairs.pair_note: Respectful, broad and clean.

hints.reason: EASTER via Easter egg hunts; SECRET via 'Easter egg' as a hidden secret in a game or film.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar phrase used in two senses; satisfying.

hints.reason: FAIRY and SUGAR together via the Sugar Plum Fairy, The Nutcracker's famous character and dance.

pairs.pair_note: Both sides come through one character name; clear and fair.

hints.reason: SPIDER via Charlotte the spider of Charlotte's Web; FARM via the Zuckerman farm barn where she saves Wilbur.

pairs.pair_note: Classic and accurate.

hints.reason: FILM via 'That's a wrap' at the end of filming; PLASTIC via plastic wrap, itself a thin film (cling film).

pairs.pair_note: Lovely double meaning with the bonus that cling film loops back to FILM.

hints.reason: FLAME via the Bunsen burner's gas flame; LAB via the burner as classic school-lab equipment.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clear clue.

hints.reason: FOOT and MOUTH together via the idiom 'put your foot in your mouth', which means making a gaffe.
hints.fix: Putting your foot in your mouth means saying something embarrassing: a gaffe.

pairs.pair_note: Good definitional aha; the MOUTH line's 'slip of the mouth' is not a real idiom, so the fix rewrites it.

hints.reason: THIN via its opposite and the phrase 'through thick and thin'; FRIEND via loyal friends through thick and thin, plus 'thick' meaning close friends ('thick as thieves').

pairs.pair_note: Instantly familiar phrase with a bonus friendship sense of 'thick'.

hints.reason: GLOVE via a gauntlet as an armored glove; MARVEL via Thanos's Infinity Gauntlet.

pairs.pair_note: Strong, thanks to the Avengers films.

hints.reason: GREEN via the Hulk's skin; STRONG via his enormous strength.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and obvious; SPINACH (green leaf, Popeye's strength) is an alternative with a little more aha, but both are good.

hints.reason: HAWK via skateboarder Tony Hawk; TIGER via Tony the Tiger of Frosted Flakes.

pairs.pair_note: Fun shared-name clue; both Tonys are household names.

hints.reason: HOLE via holey Swiss cheese; KNIFE via the Swiss Army knife; both instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join that genuinely satisfies because the HOLE side goes through cheese, not a direct compound.

hints.reason: JACK and SKELETON via Jack Skellington, the skeleton hero of The Nightmare Before Christmas.

pairs.pair_note: Clear film clue; accurate lines.

hints.reason: KITCHEN and SINK together via 'everything but the kitchen sink', an instantly familiar saying.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-based but the saying is universal and the pairing clicks.

hints.reason: LINK via clicking a link; MOUSE via the mouse click.

pairs.pair_note: Easy computing clue; fair.

hints.reason: MEMORY via 'an elephant never forgets'; TRUNK via the elephant's trunk.

pairs.pair_note: Nice mix of saying and anatomy.

hints.reason: QUEEN via the hive's queen bee; MOTHER via the true fact that the queen lays the colony's eggs, a real but less immediate second step.
hints.fix: A hive's queen bee lays nearly all its eggs, so she is mother to the colony.

pairs.pair_note: Mother side is indirect but true and clicks once explained; borderline-leaning, worth a second opinion.

hints.reason: PAN via Peter Pan; WEB via Peter Parker, Spider-Man, slinging webs (one extra step).

pairs.pair_note: Two famous Peters; satisfying once Parker clicks.

hints.reason: PRINCE via the title The Prince and the Pauper; SWITCH via the look-alike boys swapping lives.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar story; both lines accurate.

hints.reason: RECORD via an album as a record; TRACK via the songs on an album being tracks.

pairs.pair_note: Clear, honest music clue.

hints.reason: ROCK via stones being rocks and the Stones being a rock band; ROLL via the Rolling Stones (and the targets' own 'rock and roll').

pairs.pair_note: Layered: rocks, rolling, and rock 'n' roll all line up; Muddy Waters naming fact is correct.

hints.reason: SPONGEBOB via Plankton, the show's tiny villain; SECRET via his endless schemes to steal the secret Krabby Patty formula.

pairs.pair_note: Broad cartoon reference; accurate.

hints.reason: SKIN via snakes shedding skin (verb); TOOL via a tool shed (noun).

pairs.pair_note: Classic verb/noun double meaning.

hints.reason: STREET via Sesame Street; THIEF via 'open sesame' opening the forty thieves' cave in Ali Baba.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent aha; both references are widely known.
